fluff.overview: The Simian is a medium-class Inner Sphere battle armor designed for mass production and easy maintenance. Conceived under a Republic of the Sphere program to reduce the rising cost of powered infantry, the suit prioritizes affordability and field serviceability over technological sophistication. Rhodes Foundry of Devil's Rock brought the design into production in 3135, creating a general-purpose combat suit built entirely from standard Inner Sphere components. Jump-capable and equipped with magnetic claws for anti-vehicle operations, the Simian fills a skirmisher role, relying on speed and agility rather than heavy armor to protect its operators. A modular weapon mount allows field-level customization of the primary armament.
fluff.capabilities:
This configuration replaces the standard weapon with a Flamer on the modular mount, trading ranged precision for area-denial and anti-infantry capability. The flamer proves devastating in confined spaces and against unarmored targets, making this loadout well suited to urban clearance and building-to-building fighting. Magnetic claws on both arms provide melee capability and allow troopers to conduct swarming attacks against larger targets. A searchlight is also fitted.

Weighing one thousand kilograms with 350 kilograms of standard armor, the suit maintains the medium weight classification shared across all Simian configurations. The armor provides adequate protection against small arms fire but cannot absorb hits from dedicated anti-armor weapons. Above-average ground speed and a 90-meter jump range give troopers the mobility to close rapidly with targets, which complements the flamer's short effective range. This variant sees frequent use in close-assault roles where the combination of fire, speed, and magnetic claws overwhelms defenders.
fluff.deployment: Six-trooper formations carrying flamers maximized the number of area-denial weapons per unit, making them particularly effective in tunnel clearing and facility defense. The larger formation size allowed teams to advance through structures methodically while maintaining a reserve element. Organizations using Level I doctrine favored this loadout for internal security operations.
fluff.history:
The Simian emerged from a Republic of the Sphere initiative to reduce the prohibitive cost of battle armor production. Paladin Kara Rutherford championed the program, commissioning a design study that prioritized affordability and ease of maintenance over advanced technology. Rutherford did not live to see the project reach fruition. Rhodes Foundry on Devil's Rock brought the suit into production in 3135, working behind the secrecy of the Republic's collapsing borders.

The suit entered service as a tool of Exarch Jonah Levin's campaign to destabilize the Republic's rivals through deniable operations. Substantial numbers were manufactured in the months before April 3136, and troopers wearing the Simian fought across every realm bordering the Republic in false-flag formations. During campaigns in the Draconis March, RAF units masquerading as Davion forces employed Simians extensively alongside conventional forces. On Galatea in 3144, disguised Republic operatives used small craft to insert platoons of Simians directly onto Jade Falcon positions. The suit's deliberate simplicity, using common Inner Sphere components and standard weaponry, meant that virtually any industrial base could replicate it. This proliferation ensured the Simian spread well beyond Republic control as the Dark Age conflicts intensified.
